originalFinding.title: POSIX literal backslash roots are conflated with distinct nested directories
originalFinding.trigger: Register distinct POSIX directories /srv/alpha\beta and /srv/alpha/beta, with a native project whose only root is /srv/alpha\beta. Open its edit form and enable replacement of directory scope.
originalFinding.impact: sameRoot reports equality because normalizedRoot unconditionally replaces backslashes. The actual form preselects both registered project IDs, and saving sends both IDs to nativeProject/update, unintentionally broadening category metadata. It also falsely labels the other path registered and offers unrelated project categories in the thread association picker. This is a metadata-selection defect, not evidence of filesystem authorization bypass.
evidence: Direct import of the frozen sameRoot returned true for /srv/alpha\beta vs /srv/alpha/beta, while the new POSIX auto path contract treats backslash as a literal filename character.
NativeProjects.tsx:74-77 filters registered projectIds with sameRoot; 285-304 renders those IDs as prechecked boxes; 106-118 submits them unchanged after explicit scope replacement.

.work/v230-round3-web-repro.test.ts actual component reproduction produced checked=[true,true] and nativeProject/update.params.projectIds=[literal,nested], expected=[literal]. Captured request in .work/v230-round3-web-repro-evidence.json.
NativeProjects.tsx:177 uses the same comparator for registration text. ThreadOrganization.tsx:236-238 uses it to admit available project categories.
Current organization.test.tsx:194-195 covers Windows case/slash compatibility and POSIX case sensitivity, but not literal POSIX backslash identity.
originalFinding.recommendation: Keep slash-leading POSIX paths literal. Apply Windows separator and case rules only for explicit Windows drive roots or backslash UNC roots, and cover all comparator callers with regression cases.

reasoning: windowsRoot detects only drive-absolute or backslash-UNC roots. Slash-leading POSIX paths retain literal backslashes and case. sameRoot also requires equal syntax classes, preventing normalized UNC strings from aliasing POSIX //server/share.
Slash-only roots stay nonempty, empty roots never compare equal, and drive roots preserve their trailing separator. Explicit Windows case/separator compatibility remains.
All three production comparator calls revisited: NativeProjects initial projectIds selection, its registration indicator, and ThreadOrganization available project options.

The complete changed organization test file was read, including 12 direct comparator pairs and actual NativeProjects/ThreadOrganization POSIX-root, literal-backslash, drive and UNC cases. Author evidence is separate from independent execution.
